usage.drop_in: Copy the snippet's <style>, the .clip element and the <script> into a composition (for a sub-composition, inside its <template>). Give each instance a unique id. In the composition's own timeline script, before registering it, call the asset's function: gfx.<name>(tl, document.getElementById('<id>'), { at, duration, ... }). Without at/duration it reads the element's data-start and data-duration, which are local to the composition that owns tl.
usage.theming: Every color, size and position is a CSS custom property on the .clip element (--gfx-*). Override them in a style attribute or a more specific rule, with the values from frame.md. Do not edit the tweens to change colors.
usage.rules: Seekable and deterministic: one paused timeline, fromTo tweens, no Math.random, no clocks, no repeat: -1. The framework owns .clip visibility; the functions only animate children. Timing defaults follow references/graphics-and-text.md: enter at most 0.5 s before the word, content within 1 s, exit in 0.25 s.
usage.fonts: Snippets use generic families (system-ui, sans-serif). For a brand font, set --gfx-font and add the @font-face the HyperFrames linter asks for.

assets.description: Straight arrow that draws on from tail to head. Rotate it with --gfx-angle.
assets.when_to_use: Point at one UI element or value the voice names right now: anchor data-start to that word (at most 0.5 s before it). Use one arrow per idea.
assets.when_not_to_use: Not as decoration, not on something the cursor already points at, and not several arrows at once on a busy screen. If the target needs a frame, use box-highlight or ring-highlight.
assets.source: Original work for this repository (agent-video-editor), hand-written SVG/HTML/CSS/GSAP.
assets.options: at, duration (default: the element's data-start and data-duration)

assets.description: Curved arrow that draws on along a smooth arc. Flip it with --gfx-flip: -1 and rotate it with --gfx-angle.
assets.when_to_use: Point at a target from text or a label placed beside it, or link two things on screen ("this value goes here"). Anchor it to the word that names the target.
assets.when_not_to_use: Not for a straight short hop (use arrow-straight) and not to show a process with several steps (use a diagram).
assets.source: Original work for this repository (agent-video-editor), hand-written SVG/HTML/CSS/GSAP.
assets.options: at, duration (default: the element's data-start and data-duration)

assets.description: Loose, marker-style arrow with a wobbly shaft, drawn on like a pen stroke.
assets.when_to_use: Informal explainers or a casual aside ("this little button") where a hand-drawn look fits the brand skin.
assets.when_not_to_use: Not in a clean, corporate skin that uses straight shapes elsewhere: mixing both styles breaks brand consistency.
assets.source: Original work for this repository (agent-video-editor), hand-written SVG/HTML/CSS/GSAP.
assets.options: at, duration (default: the element's data-start and data-duration)

assets.description: Hand-drawn loop that circles a word, number or button, drawn on in one stroke.

assets.when_not_to_use: Not around large areas (use spotlight-dim) and not to circle several things one after another in the same shot; pick the one that matters.

assets.description: Clean elliptical ring that settles in from a larger size and sends out one soft echo pulse.

assets.when_not_to_use: Not on rectangular rows or fields (use box-highlight), and no repeating pulse: one pulse is enough.

assets.when_not_to_use: Not while the frame's content is still animating in the app (wait for the result, rule 3), and not together with a zoom on the same target in the same second.

assets.description: Dims the whole frame except a rounded rectangle; the hole can move to new targets at anchored times.

assets.when_not_to_use: Not for a single small control (use a ring or arrow), not when the viewer needs to see the rest of the screen to follow along, and not combined with a zoom in the same second.

assets.description: Generic pointer cursor with a press and a double ripple at the click point.

assets.when_not_to_use: Not on top of a recording where the real cursor is already visible at that point (place only the ripple there by hiding .gfx-cursor), and not on every click: only the ones that matter.

assets.description: Background and heading for the last 5-20 s, with dashed zones where YouTube end-screen elements go: two 16:9 video zones (640x360) and one round subscribe zone, inside the title-safe area.
assets.when_to_use: The last 5-20 s of a video at least 25 s long. Hide the dashed zones with --gfx-zone: transparent if the elements cover them.
assets.when_not_to_use: Not with other graphics, lower thirds or subscribe prompts on top during those seconds: YouTube's elements need that area free.
